records.title: 10 O'Clock Staging
records.description: Two riders wait in the tall grass beside their horses, one kneeling with a rifle while the other watches from the saddle as the quiet valley stretches beyond them. The scene carries the tension and anticipation often found in narrative Western art, where patience and timing shape the unfolding story of the American frontier. © Wayne Heim

records.title: A Face That Knows
records.description: A painterly World War II portrait of an older paratrooper in a maroon beret, a scarf at his throat and a wry half-smile on his weathered face, looking directly at the camera in warm, sepia light. Grounded in WWII reenactment photography and historical authenticity, this World War II fine art photograph captures the quiet character of the Greatest Generation in the pause before the telling, where a life is carried in a face rather than in words. This wartime portrait photography piece explores heroic portraits not through combat, but through the steady grace of a man whose face has kept what the war gave it. Part of Wayne Heim's *Facing History* fine art photography series. © Wayne Heim

records.title: A Narrow Permission

The low angle, the wet grass, and the weight of the packs give the image its urgency: a run across open ground, caught at full speed. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. Two men running, and the field opening up in front of them. © Wayne Heim

records.title: At His Side
records.description: A WWII medic tends a wounded soldier lying in the grass in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. The medic kneels over the prone man with his hands on his chest, leaning in close, while another soldier kneels behind them watching, and more men lie flat in the grass beyond. The long grass, the low crouch of the medic, and the stillness of the wounded man give the image its gravity: field aid in the open, with nothing between the men and the ground they are lying on. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. A medic at work, and a man holding on. © Wayne Heim

records.title: At the Rail
records.description: A black and white World War II battle photography image capturing WWII soldiers leaning on the rail of a landing craft, looking out at a dark sea and heavy clouds, one man's hand gripping the rail as the boat carries them toward shore. This WWII combat photography scene reflects battlefield moments and wartime action photography rooted in the Second World War, where the crossing itself is the moment, and the men at the rail have already committed to the far side. Part of a broader body of WWII battle photography and war zone photography, the composition places the backs of helmets and packs against the open water and the piled clouds, the dark sea filling the frame beyond the rail. Through restrained light and documentary realism, the image reflects the quiet resolve found in scenes from the front during World War II, grounded in historical reenactment and wartime action. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Behind the Hedgehog
records.description: American soldiers crouch behind a steel hedgehog obstacle on a beach, one aiming his rifle across a beam while another grins from behind it, their helmets netted against the grey sky. The painterly color treatment holds the frame in warm, muted tones — the sand, the khaki uniforms, and the dark steel of the hedgehog all carrying the same soft light. Part of a broader body of painterly fine art photography, this World War II frame holds the hedgehog minute: the steel crossing the frame, the rifles up behind it, and the grins holding out while the waiting goes on. The hedgehog stays where it is, and the men stay behind it, and the ground ahead stays quiet. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Behind the Wire
records.description: A young WWII soldier in a netted steel helmet looks straight at the camera from behind barbed wire in this painterly World War II portrait photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. The man sits with his hands holding a small object, the wire crossing the frame in front of him and the camouflage netting behind him, his direct gaze meeting the viewer. The wire, the net, and the man's stare give the image its tension: a portrait taken through a barrier. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. A man behind wire, and the look that gets through it. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Between the Lines
records.description: A painterly portrait photograph of a World War II servicewoman in a service cap and tie, working at a typewriter with papers spread before her and a mug at her elbow. This is painterly portrait photography at its most honest — a wartime portrait of service behind the lines, rendered as painterly fine art photography in Wayne Heim's Facing History series. Part of Wayne Heim's Facing History fine art photography series. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Between Two Men
records.description: Two German soldiers lead a wounded comrade with bandaged eyes between them in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. The wounded German soldier walks with a white bandage over his eyes, his head bowed, supported on one side by a German soldier in a steel helmet with a rifle on his back, and on the other by a German soldier in a field cap with a red-cross armband. The bandaged eyes, the two supporting hands, and the men's bowed heads give the image its gravity: a wounded man led by his comrades, with the ground ahead a place he cannot see. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. A wounded man between two comrades, and the dark in front of him. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Crossing the Open
records.description: A line of WWII soldiers advances over a rocky, grass-tufted crest in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. In the foreground a soldier in a steel helmet carries his rifle across the slope at a run, while the men behind him climb the ridge on their hands and knees and one man lies prone at the edge of the frame. The broken ground, the dust, and the angle of the climb give the image its tension: an advance caught in the open, between one piece of cover and the next. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. A moment of movement over open ground. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Cut by Water
records.description: Cut by Water is a painterly international landscape photograph captured in Iceland, where geology and weather shape the land through endurance rather than spectacle. This fine art landscape photograph reflects Wayne Heim’s approach to international landscape photography — focusing on atmosphere, restraint, and the slow narrative written by time. Light, tone, and composition emphasize the relationship between stone and movement, allowing the land itself to carry the story. Influenced by painterly European landscape traditions, the image presents nature as a process rather than an event. Part of Wayne Heim’s International – Across Borders series, this work invites sustained viewing and quiet reflection. © Wayne Heim

The lead soldier, in a netted steel helmet, aims his rifle out across the grass from behind the barrel, while the second soldier leans over his back, half out in the open, a large pipe and a tree behind them. The shared barrel, the leaning man, and the grass around them give the image its tension: two men, one piece of cover, and the open ground on every side. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. Two men, one barrel, and the open ground on every side. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Down the Track
records.description: A black and white World War II battle photography image capturing a column of WWII soldiers walking away from the camera along a bright dirt track between grassy banks and trees, packs on their backs and rifles slung, the lead man setting the pace. This WWII combat photography scene reflects battlefield moments and wartime action photography rooted in the Second World War, where the march is the mission and the men walk it together. Part of a broader body of WWII battle photography and war zone photography, the composition follows the backs of the column as the track runs between the trees, the bright dirt and the dark foliage framing the men's slow advance. Through restrained light and documentary realism, the image reflects the endurance found in scenes from the front during World War II, grounded in historical reenactment and wartime action. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Face to the Sky
records.description: Two WWII soldiers tend a wounded comrade lying on a grassy slope in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. One man sits at the wounded man's head, holding his shoulders, while the other leans over him holding his arm, the wounded man's face turned up to the sky with his mouth open, the soft haze of the image keeping the moment quiet. The two men's low crouch, the wounded man's upturned face, and the grass of the slope give the image its gravity: a moment of care on the ground where he fell. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. Two men over one man, and the face turned up to the sky. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Field Aid
records.description: A black and white World War II battlefield image capturing a medic tending to a wounded soldier in the midst of combat. The scene highlights a quieter side of the Second World War, where battlefield moments were not only defined by fighting, but by the urgent acts of care that unfolded between soldiers under fire. Part of a broader body of WWII battle photography and war zone photography, the composition emphasizes the humanity found within wartime action. Through restrained light and documentary realism, the image reflects the role of medics and the fragile seconds that shaped countless scenes from the front during the Second World War. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Find cover!
records.description: British soldiers in netted steel helmets and khaki battledress come ashore on a sandy beach from a landing craft, rifles and heavy packs on their backs, scurrying for cover as another soldier waves them on from the water's edge. The painterly color treatment keeps the frame in pale, seaside tones — the sand, the grey-green sea, and the olive-brown wool of the uniforms all holding the same flat, salt-air light. Part of a broader body of painterly fine art photography, this World War II frame is a portrait of the first minutes ashore — the ramp down, the packs on, and a beach that has to be crossed before it can be held. The sea lets them go, and the beach takes them in. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Finding Cover
records.description: American soldiers run across open ground toward cover, rifles in hand and packs on their backs, the man in front leading the line at a run while others follow with their weapons ready. The painterly color treatment holds the frame in warm, muted tones — the sand, the khaki uniforms, and the dark metal of the rifles all carrying the same soft light. Part of a broader body of painterly fine art photography, this World War II frame holds the run to cover: the rifles in hand, the packs on the backs, and the ground ahead running open to the tree line. The dust stays behind them, and the line stays running, and the cover stays ahead. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Going In
records.description: Five WWII soldiers walk across an open grassy field, seen from behind, in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. The men move in a loose line away from the camera, helmets and full packs on their backs, rifles slung over their shoulders, crossing wet grass under a pale sky. The view from behind — packs and helmets and the field ahead — gives the image its weight: a squad on the move, with the field ahead and the morning still quiet. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. A squad walking away, and the field ahead of them. © Wayne Heim

records.title: In Profile
records.description: A WWII servicewoman in uniform stands in side profile in this painterly World War II portrait photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. The woman, in a garrison cap and buttoned jacket, turns her head to the side and holds a small object up between her fingers, a slight smile on her face, a crowd of people blurred behind her, the whole image given a vintage postcard-style treatment with a faded border. The profile, the raised hand, and the smile give the image its warmth: a portrait taken from the side. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. A servicewoman in profile, and the smile the camera kept. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Inevitable
records.description: A lone rifleman pauses among towering canyon walls as a narrow beam of light cuts through the stone, isolating him in a moment of quiet vigilance. Dust clings to leather and rock alike while the figure studies the distance, the landscape itself seeming to hold its breath. Rendered in the atmospheric style of fine art Western photography, the scene reflects the tension and solitude that defined life along the American frontier-where every shadow might carry a story and every decision echoed through the silence. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Inside the Blue Silence
records.description: Inside the Blue Silence is a painterly international landscape photograph created in Iceland, where ice becomes architecture and light becomes atmosphere. This fine art landscape photograph reflects Wayne Heim’s approach to international landscape photography — treating place as an interior experience shaped by permanence rather than spectacle. Subtle tonal transitions and restrained composition create a cinematic stillness rooted in geological time. Drawing from painterly European landscape traditions, the image presents ice not as subject but as space — a vessel for light, silence, and duration. Part of Wayne Heim’s International – Across Borders series, this work invites slow viewing and sustained presence. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Kneeling in Straw
records.description: A German soldier in a steel helmet kneels in dry straw and aims a long bolt-action rifle across a pale field in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. The man leans forward on one knee, his mouth open and the rifle held out in front of him, the straw bending under his knee and the ammunition pouches at his belt. The pale straw, the long rifle, and the man's low crouch give the image its tension: an aim made from a kneeling position in a field the color of his uniform. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. A man kneeling in straw, and the shot at the far end of the field. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Left to the Weather
records.description: A painterly fine art landscape photograph set in the Mountain West, this image captures a weathered homestead resting quietly within an open western landscape. records.title: Lives Between Tides
records.description: Lives Between Tides is a painterly international landscape photograph made in the Faroe Islands, where human settlement exists in constant negotiation with sea, weather, and terrain. This fine art landscape photograph reflects Wayne Heim’s approach to international landscape photography — treating place as lived experience rather than destination. Muted light, restrained color, and careful composition create a cinematic stillness rooted in daily rhythm and survival. Influenced by painterly European landscape traditions, the image presents an inhabited world shaped by necessity and patience. Part of Wayne Heim’s International – Across Borders series, this work invites slow viewing and sustained presence. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Loaded and Ready
records.description: A painterly portrait photograph of a World War II infantryman in a netted helmet, loaded with full field gear — grenades and a canteen on crossed straps — his gaze turned to the side. The light falls across his shoulders, the gear gives the frame its texture, and the painterly handling of tone gives the portrait the quiet weight of a man carrying everything he owns into the day. This is painterly portrait photography at its most direct — a wartime portrait of the loaded infantryman, rendered as painterly fine art photography in Wayne Heim's Facing History series. Part of Wayne Heim's Facing History fine art photography series. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Loaded Down
records.description: A WWII soldier in full pack and helmet moves forward across open ground in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. The soldier carries a heavy pack on his back and a rifle slung over his shoulder, his mouth open and his gaze to the right, with a second soldier just behind him. The pale ground, the weight of the kit, and the man's mid-stride exertion give the image its force: a soldier on the move, loaded down and still going. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. A laden soldier, mid-stride, and the ground still ahead. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Low and Fast
records.description: A WWII soldier runs through tall grass with his rifle held flat across his body in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. The man leans forward into the run, pack on his back and rifle in both hands, while two more soldiers run behind him at the edge of the field. The lean of his body, the flat rifle, and the grass under his boots give the image its speed: a run with the rifle ready but not yet aimed. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. A run with the rifle flat across his body, and the trees where the running stops. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Momentary Cover
records.description: An American soldier in a netted steel helmet and olive drab uniform kneels behind a steel hedgehog anti-tank obstacle on a sandy beach, his rifle held upright in both hands, another soldier partially visible behind him. The painterly color treatment keeps the frame in pale, sandy tones — the steel of the obstacle, the olive uniform, and the pale sky all holding the same flat, sun-bleached light. Part of a broader body of painterly fine art photography, this World War II frame is a study in cover that was never meant for a man — the hedgehog built for tanks, and the soldier borrowing it for a morning. He stays low until the beach gives him a reason to move. © Wayne Heim

records.title: No Argument With Gravity
records.description: A painterly fine art waterfall photograph shaped by movement, mass, and inevitability, where water descends through rugged terrain without interruption. Rather than emphasizing scale alone, this image focuses on the relationship between gravity and form — water yielding completely to motion while stone remains unmoved. Rooted in painterly water photography, the composition treats the waterfall as an expression of certainty rather than drama. Tone, texture, and flow guide the eye downward, allowing the viewer to experience the scene as a continuous passage rather than a frozen event. Created for collectors drawn to waterfall landscape photography and painterly river scenes that emphasize presence over spectacle. © Wayne Heim

records.title: One Round Gone
records.description: A WWII soldier aims and fires his rifle on a grassy slope in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. The man stands mid-stride, rifle raised to his shoulder and pointed ahead, a spent cartridge casing hanging in the air behind him, while a second soldier's rifle shows at the edge of the frame. The lean of his body, the slope under his boots, and the casing in the air give the image its tension: a shot taken on the move. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. A shot taken on the move, and the casing still in the air. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Over the Hedgehog
records.description: A WWII soldier climbs over a large steel anti-tank obstacle in a smoky field in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. The soldier, in a steel helmet and full pack with his rifle slung on his back, has one boot on a beam of the crossed-steel obstacle while smoke fills the ground beyond it. The crossed steel, the smoke, and the man's mid-climb balance give the image its tension: an obstacle built for tanks, crossed by a man on foot. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. Steel built for tanks, crossed by a man. © Wayne Heim

This WWII combat photography scene reflects battlefield moments and wartime action photography rooted in the Second World War, where the landing is still ahead of them and the craft is the last solid ground they will stand on. Part of a broader body of WWII battle photography and war zone photography, the composition fills the frame with the backs of helmets and the crush of men, leaving no open ground in sight. Through restrained light and documentary realism, the image reflects the tension found in scenes from the front during World War II, grounded in historical reenactment and wartime action. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Path to Righteousness
records.description: A painterly fine art landscape photograph of a narrow green lane leading toward a solitary white church on the open plains of the American West. Approached with painterly restraint, the composition uses symmetry, distance, and repetition to create quiet tension rather than spectacle. The fenced path becomes a psychological device — guiding the eye forward while asking what is lost along the way. Light, tone, and space treat the landscape as emotional geography shaped by belief, habit, and time. Part of Wayne Heim’s Western American landscape photography series. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Pointing Down
records.description: A WWII soldier kneels behind a stone wall and points down at a prone comrade in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. The soldier, in a netted steel helmet with a submachine gun in one hand, points with his other arm and shouts, while the man in the grass in the foreground lies face down, his rifle on his back. The stone wall, the wet grass, and the pointing arm give the image its tension: a man down in the open, and the men behind the wall learning about him. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. A man down in the grass, and an arm pointing at him. © Wayne Heim

records.description: A black and white WWII fine art photograph of two soldiers working a Bofors anti-aircraft gun, one standing at the sight and one seated in the gunner's seat at the controls. The picture turns on the pair at two heights, with the gun's long barrel rising above them and the tented camp behind giving the waiting a place to stand. Captured by Wayne Heim for the Facing History series, the frame makes the gunner and his machine one working figure — WWII military equipment and the discipline that makes it ready. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Pressed and Waiting
records.description: A black and white World War II portrait capturing a quiet moment before departure, as a woman prepares a soldier’s uniform in soft window light. Part of Wayne Heim's Facing History fine art photography series, this painterly WWII image emphasizes anticipation, duty, and the unseen emotional weight carried on the home front. Through restrained composition and documentary-inspired realism, the photograph reflects themes of service, sacrifice, and wartime connection central to Greatest Generation storytelling. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Ready, Aim
records.description: A line of WWII soldiers kneels in tall grass with rifles aimed in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. In the foreground a soldier in a steel helmet kneels and aims his rifle across the field, while the men behind him — kneeling and prone in the grass — hold the same line, their rifles trained on the treeline at the far end. The wet grass, the low crouch of the line, and the stillness before the shot give the image its tension: a firing line caught in the breath before it fires. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. A firing line in the grass, and the shot not yet taken. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Rifle Across
records.description: A WWII soldier kneels on one knee in a grassy field with his rifle held across his body in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. The soldier wears a steel helmet and holds a bolt-action rifle in both hands, looking off to the left, while two more soldiers move through the field and the trees behind him. The kneeling pose, the rifle held across his body, and the men moving past him give the image its tension: one man stopped, the rest still going. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. One man stopped, and the rest still going. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Shading His Eyes
records.description: A young American soldier in a netted steel helmet and olive drab uniform shades his eyes with one hand as he scans the horizon, a rifle in his other hand and a pack on his back. The painterly color treatment keeps the frame in pale, washed-out tones — the khaki uniform, the web belt, and the dusty, featureless backdrop all holding the same flat, sun-bleached light. Part of a broader body of painterly fine art photography, this World War II frame is a study in looking without seeing — one man, one hand against the glare, and a horizon that gives up nothing for free. The horizon does not answer, and he keeps looking. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Soft Descent
records.description: Soft Descent is a painterly fine art landscape photograph that captures a restrained waterfall tucked beneath a dense forest canopy, where motion is gentle and atmosphere outweighs spectacle. records.title: Standing in Camp
records.description: A WWII soldier in a beret and camouflage smock stands on a camp path in this painterly World War II portrait photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. The man, a large pack on his back and a rifle slung over his shoulder, looks at the camera, sandbag revetments and tents behind him, a patch on his sleeve. The beret, the pack, and the camp behind him give the image its gravity: a portrait of a soldier, standing in camp. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. records.title: Sweat and Wire
records.description: An American soldier in a steel helmet and glasses stands over a fallen comrade lying face down on the ground, his hand wiping the sweat from his brow, barbed wire and wooden stakes filling the ground behind them. The painterly color treatment holds the frame in warm, muted tones — the khaki uniform, the worn leather of the web belt, and the pale, hazy backdrop all carrying the same soft light. Part of a broader body of painterly fine art photography, this World War II frame holds the moment after the obstacle: the wire still there, the stakes still there, and the man on the ground still there, and nothing left for the standing man to do but wipe his brow. The wire stays where it is, and the man stays where he is, and the hand stays on the brow. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Taking a Knee
records.description: A WWII soldier kneels on one knee in the grass with his rifle planted beside him in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. The soldier wears a steel helmet and a full pack, a patch on his sleeve, and looks off to the left while the rifle stands upright in the grass and the trees stand still behind him. The kneeling pose, the planted rifle, and the quiet field give the image its gravity: a pause on the move, held on one knee. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. One knee in the grass, and the field holding still. © Wayne Heim

records.title: The Automatic
records.description: An American soldier in a steel helmet stands in profile in low brush, an automatic rifle held across his body and a heavy pack on his back, his eyes on the ground ahead of him. The painterly color treatment holds the frame in warm, muted tones — the khaki uniform, the worn wood of the rifle, and the pale, hazy brush all carrying the same soft light. Part of a broader body of painterly fine art photography, this World War II frame holds the brush walk: the automatic up, the pack high, and the eyes working the ground the brush is hiding. The brush stays around him, and the automatic stays up, and the ground ahead stays hidden. © Wayne Heim

records.title: The Barrels
records.description: Two men in civilian clothes take cover behind wooden barrels in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. One man kneels behind a barrel with his rifle resting on its rim, aiming out across the grass, while the second man watches from behind the next barrel, a rough stone wall at their backs. The oak barrels, the stone wall, and the men's flat caps give the image its character: an improvised firing position, held by men in their own clothes. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. Two men, two barrels, and a wall at their backs. © Wayne Heim

records.title: The Braced Shot
records.description: A WWII soldier fires a rifle from behind a wooden barrel in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. The soldier, in a steel helmet with a canteen at his belt, crouches low behind a large oak barrel, his rifle braced on its rim and aimed out across the grass, a tree standing behind him. The oak barrel, the braced rifle, and the man's low crouch give the image its tension: a shot fired from improvised cover, with the grass open in front of him. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. A shot from behind a barrel, and the grass open in front of him. © Wayne Heim

records.title: The Carry
records.description: A WWII soldier carries a wounded comrade across a field on his back in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. The carrier moves through long grass with the wounded man's head hanging down against his shoulder, his rifle in one hand, while a second soldier lies flat in the grass behind them. Anti-tank obstacles and a fence stand in the background, and the open ground between them and the far hedge gives the image its weight: a rescue in progress, with the far hedge still a long way off. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. A man carried, and a long way to go. © Wayne Heim

records.title: The Charge
records.description: American soldiers charge forward in a wide line across open ground, rifles at the ready with bayonets fixed and packs on their backs, dust rising around them under a hazy sky. The painterly color treatment holds the frame in warm, muted tones — the khaki uniforms, the dark metal of the rifles, and the pale dust all carrying the same soft light. Part of a broader body of painterly fine art photography, this World War II frame holds the charge itself: the line going forward together, the bayonets pointing the way, and the far side still ahead of them. The dust stays thick, and the line stays wide, and the far side stays ahead. © Wayne Heim

records.title: The Crouching Man
records.description: Two German soldiers surrender in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. Seen from behind, one man stands with both arms raised high, a checkered scarf waving in his raised hand, while the other crouches low in the foreground beside him, helmet down and hands out of sight. The raised arms, the waving scarf, and the crouched man's low shape give the image its gravity: a surrender shown from the crouching man's side, with no weapon in sight. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. Two men, one scarf, and the crouch underneath the wave. © Wayne Heim

records.title: The Drag
records.description: A WWII soldier drags a wounded comrade across dusty ground in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. The standing man leans forward, hands locked around the fallen man's arms, the man's boots trailing in the dirt behind them while dust rises around their feet. A lone figure stands in the distance, watching from too far away to help. The drag, the dust, and the two lines in the dirt give the image its weight: a rescue measured in steps. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. A man dragged out of the dust, one pull at a time. © Wayne Heim

records.title: The Flag Patch
records.description: An American soldier in a netted steel helmet points to the right from behind wooden barrels in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. The soldier holds his rifle vertically in one hand, butt on the ground, and points with two fingers of the other, a US flag patch on his sleeve and a pouch strapped to his chest, while a second soldier crouches behind him, a large pipe and a barrel in the background. The pointing arm, the flag patch, and the rifle held down at his side give the image its tension: a direction given, with the ground it points to out of frame. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. A flag on a sleeve, and a finger pointing right. © Wayne Heim

records.title: The Ford
records.description: Two WWII soldiers ford a shallow stream in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. The cold water, the mud, and the low crouch of the crossing give the image its tension: a ford in the open, with the far bank still to reach. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. records.title: The Foxhole
records.description: A black and white World War II battle photography image capturing a German soldier in a steel helmet slumped in a foxhole, leaning back against the earthen wall with a submachine gun across his knees, his mouth open as he shouts. This WWII combat photography scene reflects battlefield moments and wartime action photography rooted in the Second World War, where the dirt wall is the wall he has, and the shelling is the sound he lives with. Part of a broader body of WWII battle photography and war zone photography, the composition frames the soldier low against the dirt wall, the dark helmet and the weapon dark against the pale earth. Through restrained light and documentary realism, the image reflects the strain found in scenes from the front during World War II, grounded in historical reenactment and wartime action. © Wayne Heim

The front man's walk, the crouching men, and the prone man give the image its shape: a group in every posture a trench has. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. records.title: The Gun Crew

The backs of the two men, the wheels of the gun, and the barrel against the sky give the image its gravity: a gun crew at rest between firings. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. records.description: An American sergeant with three chevrons on his sleeve laughs in a snowy forest, a BAR held across his arms and leather gloves on his hands, his helmet netted against the trees and other soldiers moving through the snow behind him. records.title: The Laughing Carry
records.description: A WWII soldier grins as he carries a comrade on his back in this painterly World War II photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. The carrier, in a netted steel helmet and camouflage smock, laughs under the weight of the man on his back, the carried man's legs dangling and his arms around the carrier's shoulders, a patch on the carrier's sleeve. The grin, the dangling legs, and the two men's full kit give the image its warmth: a carry that is a laugh, not a rescue. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. A man carrying a man, and the grin under the weight. © Wayne Heim

records.title: The Medic's Hands
records.description: A medic in a steel helmet with a red-cross armband kneels in the mud over a wounded soldier lying on his back, his hands at the man's chest, a medical bag at his side. The painterly color treatment keeps the frame in grey-green, muddy tones — the netted helmet, the worn field jacket, and the pale, still face of the wounded man all holding the same flat, overcast light. Part of a broader body of painterly fine art photography, this World War II frame is a study in the quiet work — one medic, one wounded man, and a patch of mud that has become the whole war for both of them. The medic stays on his knees, and the wounded man stays breathing. © Wayne Heim

records.title: The Overhead Carry
records.description: Three WWII soldiers move across sandy ground in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. The center man lifts a long weapon above his head with both hands, arms raised and mouth open, while a second soldier crouches beside him gripping a rifle and a third walks behind them with a rifle slung. The raised weapon, the crouching man, and the sandy ground give the image its momentum: a hoist on the move. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. Three men, one long weapon, and the arms up above his head. © Wayne Heim

records.title: The Paper by the Fire
records.description: A woman in a red snood and a pale blue dress sits in an armchair by a fireplace, reading a newspaper whose headline reports the D-Day landings, a framed photograph of a young soldier on the mantel beside a radio. The painterly color treatment keeps the frame in warm, domestic tones — the dark wood of the mantel, the red of the snood, and the soft light of the room all holding the same muted, late-afternoon glow. Part of a broader body of painterly fine art photography, this World War II frame is a portrait of the war as it reaches a living room — one woman, one newspaper, and a photograph that never leaves the mantel. She reads the headline a third time. © Wayne Heim

records.title: The Pause Inside the Weather
records.description: This painterly fine art mountain photograph from the Mountain West captures a fleeting moment of light moving across snow-covered peaks during a winter storm. Rendered with restrained contrast, muted tonality, and atmospheric depth, the image reflects a painterly landscape photography approach focused on weather as presence rather than event. Rooted in western landscape photography, the composition emphasizes mass, endurance, and quiet interruption. Light does not dominate the scene; it passes through it. The work invites sustained viewing, where tension and stillness coexist without resolution. Part of Wayne Heim’s Western American landscape photography series. © Wayne Heim

records.title: The Raised Hand
records.description: A young WWII soldier in a netted steel helmet signals with a raised hand in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. The soldier kneels behind a low earth bank, his right arm raised and his mouth open as he calls out, a dark patch on his sleeve and his rifle slung at his back. The open mouth, the raised hand, and the dirt on his uniform give the image its urgency: a signal given in the open, with the men behind him out of frame. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. A raised hand, and a voice carrying. © Wayne Heim

records.title: The Shout
records.description: A WWII soldier shouts with his fist raised high in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. The soldier, in a netted steel helmet with a grenade at his chest, holds a submachine gun in one hand and raises a clenched fist with the other, his mouth open, a stone wall at his back and smoke in front of him. The raised fist, the open mouth, and the weapon pointed at the sky give the image its force: a signal given loud, with the men behind him out of frame. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. A fist in the air, and a voice behind it. © Wayne Heim

records.title: The Strap
records.description: Two German soldiers stand in a smoky landscape in this painterly World War II portrait photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. In the foreground a young German soldier in a gray uniform and field cap adjusts the strap across his chest, ammunition pouches at his belt, while a second German soldier stands behind him wearing sunglasses and a field cap. The pale smoke, the young soldier's half-turned pose, and the watching man behind him give the image its tension: a pair of soldiers caught in a quiet moment before the next move. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. Two German soldiers, and a strap that will not sit right. © Wayne Heim

records.title: The Trench Walk
records.description: A WWII soldier walks down a narrow earth trench in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. Seen from behind, the man carries a pack loaded with a coiled rope, a hanging mug, netting, and pouches, while another soldier lies in the trench ahead of him, the earth walls close on both sides. The pack, the rope, and the narrow earth walls give the image its weight: a walk through ground the trench has already made. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. A man walking under his pack, and the trench on both sides of him. © Wayne Heim

Part of a broader body of painterly fine art photography, this World War II frame holds the aftermath: the shooting done, the beach quiet, and one man walking through the obstacles with his weapon across his shoulders. records.description: Two WWII soldiers lean on a low stone wall and look over it in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. Seen from behind, the men rest their arms on the wall, packs on their backs and rifles on their shoulders, the grassy field beyond the wall and the stone under their arms. The lean, the wall, and the field beyond give the image its gravity: a watch kept from a low stone wall. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. Two men on a wall, and the field beyond it. © Wayne Heim

records.title: They Are Coming
records.description: A young American soldier in a netted steel helmet rises halfway out of a foxhole, his rifle held upright in one hand, his eyes fixed on the ground beyond the rim. The painterly color treatment holds the frame in warm, muted tones — the sand of the foxhole, the olive drab of his uniform, and the pale, cloudy sky all carrying the same soft light. Part of a broader body of painterly fine art photography, this World War II frame holds the foxhole minute, when a man is half in the ground and half out of it, watching ground that has not moved yet. The rifle stays up, and the rim stays under his chest, and the ground beyond it stays quiet. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Three for One
records.description: Three medics tend a wounded soldier on the sand in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. One medic kneels over the man, his hands at the wound, while the other two lean in from either side, a rifle lying on the ground beside them and a medic's bag at the foreground. The red-cross armbands, the low crouch of the three men, and the wounded man's stillness give the image its gravity: a moment of care in the middle of the fight. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. Three men around one wound, and the fight set down beside them. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Together on the Tank
records.description: Six WWII soldiers pose together on and around a tank in this painterly World War II photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. The men stand, sit, and lean on the tank — one perched on the turret, others grouped at the hull — the white star on the tank's side and the gun barrel pointing to the left, the whole image given a vintage postcard-style treatment with a faded border. The six men's smiles, the star, and the tank's bulk give the image its warmth: a crew together on their machine. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. Six men on a tank, and the star on the side of it. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Up and Over
records.description: A dramatic black and white World War II battle photography image capturing WWII soldiers advancing over a grassy rise as they move into open ground, one man lunging ahead with his rifle while another follows close behind and a third stays low in the grass at the foot of the mound. This WWII combat photography scene reflects battlefield moments and wartime action photography rooted in the Second World War, where the rise is the last shelter and the men crossing it are already committed to the open field beyond. Part of a broader body of WWII battle photography and war zone photography, the composition emphasizes the strain and momentum of an infantry advance. Through restrained light and documentary realism, the image reflects the urgency found in scenes from the front during World War II, grounded in historical reenactment and wartime action. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Up From the Beach
records.description: A half-track armored vehicle packed with WWII soldiers comes up a sandy beach road in this painterly World War II photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. The men stand, sit, and lean over the sides of the crowded vehicle — helmets and rifles among them — the USA marking and the white star on the half-track's front, tire tracks in the sand behind it, the whole image given a vintage postcard-style treatment with a faded border. The crowded back, the vehicle's face, and the sand give the image its momentum: a full load, coming up the beach. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. A half-track full of men, and the sand coming up with it. © Wayne Heim

records.title: What's our next move?
records.description: Two American soldiers lie prone in the sand on a Normandy beach, rifles down beside them, steel hedgehogs rising all around them in the pale light. The man in front grins toward the camera while the man beside him looks off to the right, and more men crouch behind them in the haze. The painterly color treatment holds the frame in warm, muted tones — the sand, the khaki uniforms, and the netted helmets all carrying the same soft light. Part of a broader body of painterly fine art photography, this World War II frame catches the long minute under fire, when men lie low, keep their rifles close, and grin at the camera like the beach is not trying to kill them. The hedgehogs stay where they are, and the sand stays under the men, and the next move is still to be made. © Wayne Heim

records.title: With the Tank
records.description: WWII soldiers advance alongside a tank in this painterly World War II battle photograph by Wayne Heim, part of the Facing History collection. In the foreground a soldier in a steel helmet moves forward at a crouch with his rifle across his body, while the men behind him work their way out from behind sandbag walls and a tank grinds forward in the background, its gun pointed down the road. Smoke, cut-up ground, and the low crouch of the advance give the image its urgency: infantry and armor moving together, caught in the open. Part of a broader body of work, this piece is one of a series of images, crafted to honor the enduring legacy of the Facing History collection and the historical moments it represents. It is suited for collection within this narrative series, bringing depth, historical perspective, and emotion to any fine art collection or art lover's space. Infantry and armor, moving together through the smoke. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Young Aide
records.description: A young woman in a Women's Army Corps uniform - a side cap with a light piping on her head, a dark jacket with a collar badge and a shoulder insignia, a white shirt and a tie, her hair in a bun - looks off to the right with a serious expression, a blurred light background of trees behind her at D-Day Conneaut. The black-and-white portrait holds the whole moment in the looking - one woman, one cap, and a gaze that goes past everything. Traditional fine art photography. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Young Girl as Reenactor
records.description: A young girl in Civil War-era dress - a long smock with a wide collar, a knit cap, and a fingerless glove on her hand - leans on a wooden windowsill at Hale Farm with her arms folded, looking off to the side with a pensive expression, the weathered planks of a wooden building behind her. The sepia-black-and-white portrait holds the whole moment in the lean - a girl at a window, and the quiet that comes with it. Traditional fine art photography. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Young Resistance Fighter
records.description: A young woman in a floral dress, her light hair pulled back, looks off-camera with a serious, thoughtful expression, outdoors among trees at the D-Day Conneaut living-history event, in the role of a French Resistance fighter. A black-and-white traditional fine art reenactor portrait, photographed in Wayne Heim's traditional portrait style. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Young Trees
records.description: A small group of trees stands in a field beneath the shadow of the Tetons, giving the mountain landscape a quiet foreground rhythm. This traditional fine art photograph creates Western mountain wall art rooted in scale, young growth, and the stillness of open Wyoming land.

records.title: Young Warrior
records.description: A young figure stands near the water's edge, holding a staff upright as his voice breaks into the open air. His posture is lifted and expressive, with movement carried through his raised arm and open mouth. Light softens the scene while revealing detail in the headdress, beadwork, and textures of his clothing, set against the calm surface behind him. © Wayne Heim
